entradas.text: It was a cloudy, rainy day in Holsord.
The gloomy weather couldn't dampen my spirits. My constitutional reforms had passed in court. I had won.
That wasn't the only cause for excitement in the Rayne household. Today, Franc was finally leaving home.
The gloomy weather echoed my own feelings. My constitutional changes had been defeated. I was back to square one.
I couldn't spend the day moping, however. Franc was finally about to leave home.
The gloomy weather echoed my own feelings. The court had ruled against me. My presidency might be on the line.
But neither the gloomy weather, nor the unfolding protests, could dampen my spirits following my recent court win.
My son piled the last of his bags next to the door. Serge and the assistant driver were waiting outside next to the car.
"Did you pack everything?"
"Don't forget to give me a call *immediately* after you arrive."
Monica helped him put his backpack on while Serge started carrying the luggage to the car.
"I made you a sack lunch! I'll get it from the kitchen."
"Franc! Franc!"
"I'm gonna miss you."
"I'll miss you too. Don't forget, you've got to give Mom and Dad an extra hard time for both of us now."
Franc picked up his sister and gave her a big hug. Monica appeared in the doorway, holding a paper bag.
"I cut the crusts off your sandwich, just the way you used to like."
"Can't a mother pretend? Oh, Franc!"
"I'm not a kid anymore, Mom."
She embraced him with tears in her eyes. Franc looked as if he was about to cry as well.
Serge approached.
"Sir, Franc needs to catch the next flight to Arcasia which leaves from Holsord International in two hours."
"Sir, Franc needs to catch the next bus to the border in order to report for basic training on time."
"Sir, Franc needs to catch the next bus to the border to get to the military academy before roll call."
"Sir, Franc needs to catch the next ship to United Contana which leaves from Conriat Port in four hours."
"Sir, as per the schedule, Franc needs to be at Holsord State University to start his orientation in an hour."
"We will have to leave now to make it."
"Thank you, Serge."
"Time to go, Franc."
Franc turned around and took one last look at me.
"Yes, but when you do, everything will be different."
"It's difficult to see them grow and leave, isn't it?"
"Home will feel a bit empty now."
entradas.menu: "Home will feel a bit empty now."

entradas.text: "It's not like we will never see him again."
entradas.menu: "It's not like we will never see him again."

entradas.text: "He will. We all did, after all."
"That isn't the only thing that won't be the same."
"It's time for him to find himself in the world."
entradas.menu: "It is time for him to find himself in the world."

entradas.text: "Just make sure he gets there safe and sound, Serge."
entradas.menu: "Just make sure he gets there safe and sound, Serge."

entradas.text: "Of course, Mr. President."
"I think it will be a liberating experience for him. It's never easy for boys to live in the shadow of their fathers."
"And it must be even harder when one's father is Anton Rayne. A great man like you casts a very long shadow."
"That's enough, Serge. Just do your job."
entradas.menu: "That's enough, Serge. Just do your job."

entradas.text: "Well said."
"Not everyone thinks that."
"Excuse my language Mr. President, but to hell with them. You are my president, now and forever."
"As you wish, Mr. President."
He nodded and looked at his watch.
"Time to go."
He looked at his watch.
Serge looked at his watch.
Franc waved his hand as he entered the car.
Monica stood next to me as they drove away. Her eyes were teary.
Monica looked at me as if she was going to say something. She turned and headed inside.
"There he goes."
"It already feels different."
She put her head on my shoulder.
"He will be fine."
"I know."
"We still have each other."
I stroked her hair supportively.
She turned to me, kissed me on my cheek and put her head on my shoulder again.
"I know he will."
"With all the protests going on, I hope we will be alright."
I watched the car drive down the road until it was no longer in sight.
"With the recent court loss, I hope we will be alright."
"With the defeat of your reforms, I hope we will be alright."
"At least he has a father he can boast to his new friends about. *Anton the Great Reformer*. Sounds good, doesn't it?"
We watched for a few more minutes, even after the car was no longer in sight.
That wasn't the only cause for excitement in the Rayne household. Today, Franc was finally leaving home.
I couldn't spend the day moping, however. Franc was finally about to leave home.
"Mom. I'm moving less than an hour away. You'll see me all the time!"
"I know. But it won't be the same."
"I will. I think I'm all packed."
She dashed down the hall. Franc and I turned to face each other in the doorway.
"So, I guess this is it."
"I guess it is."
"I know you're still mad at me. But I made this decision for your own good."
entradas.menu: "I know you're still mad at me. But I made this decision for your own good."

entradas.text: "I guess it is."
"I guess it is."
"I guess it is."
"I know you're still mad at me. But you're going to like it at Holsord State."
entradas.menu: "I know you're still mad at me. But you're going to like it at Holsord State."

entradas.text: "Goodbye and good riddance?"
"Goodbye and good riddance?"
"I know studying abroad wasn't your first choice. But I hope you can live with it."
entradas.menu: "I know studying abroad wasn't your first choice. But I hope you can live with it."

entradas.text: "Goodbye and good riddance?"
"You're leaving the country to get away from me. I hope you're happy."
entradas.menu: "You're leaving the country to get away from me. I hope you're happy."

entradas.text: "I guess it is."
"I hope they'll teach you how to be a better shot than me."
entradas.menu: "I hope they'll teach you how to be a better shot than me."

entradas.text: "Don't forget where you came from, son."
entradas.menu: "Don't forget where you came from, son."

entradas.text: "I guess it is."
"You're going to do great."
"I know the military wasn't your first choice, but it's for your own good."
entradas.menu: "I know the military wasn't your first choice, but it's for your own good."

entradas.text: "I gave you a second chance. Don't screw this one up."
entradas.menu: "I gave you a second chance. Don't screw this one up."

entradas.text: "Something like that."
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
"That's it? That's all you have to say?"
"Yeah. Whatever."
"Something like that."
"That's it? That's all you have to say?"
"Couldn't be happier."
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
"Uh huh. Whatever."
"Something like that."
"That's it? That's all you have to say?"
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
"Look, Dad. I know I've been kind of a pill since you became President. But you haven't exactly been Father of the Year either."
"I don't want to leave on a bum note. Can we, you know, sign a peace accord? Or whatever you government people do?"
"Look, Dad. I know I've been kind of a pill since you became President. But you haven't exactly been Father of the Year either."
"I don't want to leave the country on a bum note. Can we, you know, sign a peace accord? Or whatever you government people do?"
"I don't want to leave on a bum note. I mean, who knows when I'll be back? So can we, you know, sign a peace accord? Or whatever you government people do?"
"Look, Dad. I know I've been kind of a pill since you became President. But you haven't exactly been Father of the Year either."
"Of course, Franc. I love you."
"I won't apologize for your ingrate behavior."
entradas.menu: "I won't apologize for your ingrate behavior."

entradas.text: "Just get out of my house."
"I suppose we can. But I've left my signing pen in my office."
entradas.menu: "I suppose we can. But I've left my signing pen in my office."

entradas.text: "I know. I don't blame you."
"That wouldn't be hard. I remember our one hunting trip."
"I will, don't worry."
"How could I? I'm the President's son!"
"I know. I'll actually study this time."
"Thanks, Dad."
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
"I haven't forgotten what you told me about your university years. I hope the army gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
"You still never told me about your university years, but I know I've had it easy compared to you. I hope the army gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
"You still never told me about your university years, but I know I've had it easy compared to you. I hope moving abroad gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
"I haven't forgotten what you told me about your university years. I hope going to a new country gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
"I haven't forgotten what you told me about your university years. I hope Holsord State gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
"You still never told me about your university years, but I know I've had it easy compared to you. I hope Holsord State gives me a chance to prove myself the same way you did."
Franc shifted his weight nervously.
"For your sake, I hope that chance never comes."
entradas.menu: "For your sake, I hope that chance never comes."

entradas.text: "Just don't do anything stupid."
"Don't model your life on mine. You're your own man now, Franc."
entradas.menu: "Don't model your life on mine. You're your own man now, Franc."

entradas.text: "You don't have to prove yourself to anyone. Especially not me."
entradas.menu: "You don't have to prove yourself to anyone. Especially not me."

entradas.text: Franc looked down at the ground.
Franc smiled.
"All right, Dad."
Franc scowled.
"I figured as much. Been nice knowing you, Anton."
Franc took a step back, astonished. He blinked back tears.
"I-- I love you too."
Franc smiled.
"We'll just have to shake on it, then."
At that moment, Deana rushed to the door.
"Okay."
Deana nodded.
I caught her glaring at me over his shoulder. I hoped someday she would understand why I'd decided to send him away.
I said nothing and watched him get in the back of the car.
"Good luck."
"See you soon."
"Make me proud."
Franc nodded, before heading to the car.
"The army changes a man, even if he never sees combat."
"Being exposed to a different culture, different beliefs... it changes a man."
"Living away from home, making your own choices for the first time... it changes a man."
"A military education changes a man, even if he never sees combat."
"Being exposed to a different culture, different beliefs... it changes a man."
I sighed and closed the door.
I sighed and closed the door.
"If you ever need money, don't refrain from telling us."
"You know that we have been doing very well recently."
"I know. Thanks, Mom."
The engine started and they were on their way.
